- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is negative or volatile (especially after recent spikes).  
- Underestimate downward corrections after strong upward moves; model tends to overreact to recent highs.  
- When sentiment turns positive mid-cycle, model often overshoots the true mean; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.  
- Lagged corrections (e.g., 3–5 day delays) are common; model often fails to adjust for sentiment shifts within 2–3 days.  
- Mean reversion is stronger in the 10–15 day horizon; model overweights short-term momentum, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- Avoid overconfidence in “trending” signals; sentiment-driven spikes should be capped at 1.5x the 14-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
